tests.summary: `python -m openpyxl.redact --help` runs and documents --spec and --report.
A folder of well-formed workbooks yields one readable copy per workbook and exit status zero.
A sheet named in drop_sheets is gone from the copy; the other sheets keep their order.
Columns whose headers are named in drop_columns are gone; the other columns keep their values and order.
A formula in the same sheet that used a removed cell directly shows the marker.
The report has the documented header and one row per file found under INPUT_DIR.
A clean run prints the summary line with the right counts.
redact_workbook(source, destination, spec) writes the copy and returns the report row.
Comments on kept cells survive in the copy.
The library's existing test suite still passes once the module is added.
A workbook where nothing matches is copied with its values intact and reported unchanged.
The second column with a matching header, spelt loosely, is removed too.
Removing two columns far apart removes those two, not a neighbour.
A pivot table's cache does not carry the removed column's values.
The copy carries no link to another workbook.
Document properties do not name the author or the machine.
The report never contains a removed value.
A kept cell whose text begins with '=' is still text in the copy.
A marker that begins with '=' lands as text, not as a formula.
A formula that referenced a kept column to the right of a removed one still points at the same data.
A formula on another sheet that used the removed column shows the marker, not the data that moved in.
A formula on another sheet that referenced a kept column shifts with it.
Defined names follow their ranges: a name over removed data goes, a name over kept data shifts.
A table shrinks to the columns that remain.
A merged range spanning a removed column shrinks.
Conditional formats and validations follow their columns.
Column widths and hidden flags follow their columns.
Nothing in the copy refers to a removed sheet.
An array formula over kept data survives and points at the same data.
A file already at a copy's destination is not replaced.
A symlink at a copy's destination is not followed.
Every file under INPUT_DIR is byte-identical afterwards.
An OUTPUT_DIR inside INPUT_DIR is refused.
A copy that fails during writing leaves nothing at its destination.
A spec whose list field is a string is refused before any copy is written.
A spec with an unknown field is refused before any copy is written.
The report's counts agree with the copy.
A run with a failed workbook exits non-zero and the summary agrees with the report.
An encrypted workbook that sorts first does not stop the others and is reported.
A file that is not a workbook is reported failed and the workbooks after it are processed.
